title: Which Performance in Green Certification Pays, and How? CASBEE for Real Estate Item Scores and the Economics of Japanese Office REITs
content: Green certification has been linked to higher rents and prices, but it remains unclear which certified performance attributes relate to economic outcomes, and through which channels. We examine 2,611 property-periods (2021–2026) of 426 office properties held by Japanese real estate investment trusts (J-REITs) and certified under CASBEE for Real Estate (CASBEE: Comprehensive Assessment System for Built Environment Efficiency). Hedonic regressions using property-level data from annual securities reports relate category and item scores to rent, utility cost, operating expenses, net operating income (NOI), implied cap rate, and appraisal value. Equality of coefficients across the five major categories was rejected for five of six outcomes. The Energy Use/GHG Emissions (GHG: greenhouse gas) score was associated with lower utility cost (3.2% per point) but not significantly with rent or appraisal value. The Materials/Safety score showed the largest association with appraisal value (5.3% per point), mainly through NOI. Within this category, a one-level higher score on high earthquake resistance and seismic isolation was associated with 9.7% higher appraisal value, with a lower cap rate also contributing substantially. The Indoor Environment score was not significantly associated with rent or appraisal value. Environmental performance is not uniformly linked to value; outcomes and channels differ by item.
